correctness.rationale: At stationary exponential observation times the perpetuity X=Z+UX' with Z a Brownian displacement over Exp(lambda), gives (1+kappa||t||²)phi(t)=E phi(Ut) for kappa=D/lambda. Substitution phi=(1+beta||t||²)^(-q) and coefficient comparison gives E U^(2n)=1-hn/(q+n-1), h=kappa/beta. For q<1 this violates E U4<=E U2, and as n tends to infinity it gives P(U=1)=1-h>=0. Hausdorff moment uniqueness identifies only the asserted two-atom law for q=1 or (1-h)delta1+h Beta(2q-2,1) for q>1, with q>=1, beta>=kappa. The beta integral exactly verifies the identity for all z>=0. E U²<1 ensures L² perpetuity convergence and synchronous-coupling contraction, proving unique invariant law for any finite d. Independently checked 228 exact rational moment identities plus boundaries. This depends on common scalar iid [0,1] resets, not general affine resetting.
